# The Rust Style Guide

> **Source:** [The Rust Style Guide](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/style-guide/)
>
> The default Rust style, enforced by `rustfmt`. Applies unless the Google guide overrides it (see **Google note** entries).

## [Formatting Conventions](01-formatting-conventions.md)

| ID | Title | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [RS-FMT-01](01-formatting-conventions.md#rs-fmt-01) | Indentation and line width | Indent with spaces; **MUST NOT** use tabs. Each indentation level **MUST** be 4 spaces. Lines **MUST NOT** exceed the maximum width of 100 characters. |
| [RS-FMT-02](01-formatting-conventions.md#rs-fmt-02) | Block indent | **SHOULD** prefer block indent over visual indent. |
| [RS-FMT-03](01-formatting-conventions.md#rs-fmt-03) | Trailing commas | In comma-separated lists of any kind, **MUST** use a trailing comma when the last element is followed by a newline. |
| [RS-FMT-04](01-formatting-conventions.md#rs-fmt-04) | Blank lines | **MUST** separate items and statements by either zero or one blank lines (i.e., one or two newlines). |
| [RS-FMT-05](01-formatting-conventions.md#rs-fmt-05) | Trailing whitespace | **MUST NOT** include trailing whitespace at the end of any line: blank lines, comment lines, code lines and string literals. |
| [RS-FMT-06](01-formatting-conventions.md#rs-fmt-06) | Sorting (version sorting) | Wherever the default style says to sort and specifies nothing else, sorting **MUST** be "version sorting", so that e.g. `x8` comes before `x16` even though `1` precedes `8`. |
| [RS-FMT-07](01-formatting-conventions.md#rs-fmt-07) | Comments | These are recommendations only; a mechanical formatter may skip formatting comments. **SHOULD** prefer line comments (`//`) to block comments (`/* ... */`), and **SHOULD** put a comment on its own line. |
| [RS-FMT-08](01-formatting-conventions.md#rs-fmt-08) | Doc comments | **SHOULD** prefer line doc comments (`///`) to block doc comments (`/** ... */`). **SHOULD** prefer outer doc comments (`///` or `/** ... */`); use inner doc comments (`//!` and `/*! ... */`) only for module-level or crate-level documentation. **MUST** put doc comments before attributes. |
| [RS-FMT-09](01-formatting-conventions.md#rs-fmt-09) | Attributes | **MUST** put each attribute on its own line, indented to the level of the item; inner attributes (`#!`) are indented to the level of the inside of the item. **SHOULD** prefer outer attributes where possible. |
| [RS-FMT-10](01-formatting-conventions.md#rs-fmt-10) | *Small* items | Where this guide gives formatting that depends on a construct being *small* (e.g., single-line vs multi-line struct literals), each tool decides exactly what *small* means and **MAY** use different definitions in different circumstances. |

## [Items](02-items.md)

| ID | Title | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [RS-ITEM-01](02-items.md#rs-item-01) | Item ordering | `extern crate` statements **MUST** come first in a file, ordered alphabetically. `use` statements and module *declarations* (`mod foo;`, not `mod { ... }`) **MUST** come before other items, with imports before module declarations. |
| [RS-ITEM-02](02-items.md#rs-item-02) | Function definitions | Function definitions **MUST** be formatted so that searching for `fn [function-name]` finds them, using the order and spacing `[pub] [unsafe] [extern ["ABI"]] fn foo(arg1: i32, arg2: i32) -> i32 {`. **SHOULD** avoid comments within the signature. |
| [RS-ITEM-03](02-items.md#rs-item-03) | Tuples and tuple structs | **MUST** write the type list of a tuple or tuple struct as a function parameter list ([RS-ITEM-02](02-items.md#rs-item-02)) and **MUST** build a tuple or tuple struct as a function call ([expressions](04-expressions.md)). |
| [RS-ITEM-04](02-items.md#rs-item-04) | Tuples and tuple structs: single-line | Single-line form of tuple structs, as shown below (the source gives only this example). |
| [RS-ITEM-05](02-items.md#rs-item-05) | Enums | In an enum declaration, **MUST** put each variant on its own block-indented line, formatted as a struct (without the `struct` keyword), a tuple struct, or an identifier (no special formatting). |
| [RS-ITEM-06](02-items.md#rs-item-06) | Structs and unions | The struct name **MUST** follow the `struct` keyword on the same line, with the opening brace on that line when it fits within the right margin. Fields **MUST** be indented once and each end with a trailing comma; the closing brace is unindented on its own line. |
| [RS-ITEM-07](02-items.md#rs-item-07) | Tuple structs | Put the whole tuple struct on one line if possible, separating types with a comma and a space; **MUST NOT** use a trailing comma in a single-line tuple struct, and **MUST NOT** put spaces around the parentheses or semicolon. |
| [RS-ITEM-08](02-items.md#rs-item-08) | Traits | **MUST** use block indent for trait items. A trait with no items **MUST** be formatted on a single line including its `{}`; otherwise break after the opening brace and before the closing brace. |
| [RS-ITEM-09](02-items.md#rs-item-09) | Impls | **MUST** use block indent for impl items. An impl with no items **MUST** be formatted on a single line including its `{}`; otherwise break after the opening brace and before the closing brace. |
| [RS-ITEM-10](02-items.md#rs-item-10) | Extern crate | **MUST** use spaces around keywords and **MUST NOT** put spaces around the semicolon: `extern crate foo;`. |
| [RS-ITEM-11](02-items.md#rs-item-11) | Modules | **MUST** use spaces around keywords and before the opening brace, and **MUST NOT** put spaces around the semicolon. |
| [RS-ITEM-12](02-items.md#rs-item-12) | `macro_rules!` | **MUST** use `{}` for the full definition of the macro. |
| [RS-ITEM-13](02-items.md#rs-item-13) | Generics | **SHOULD** put a generics clause on one line, breaking other parts of the item declaration rather than the generics clause. If a generics clause is large enough to require line-breaking, **SHOULD** prefer a `where` clause instead. |
| [RS-ITEM-14](02-items.md#rs-item-14) | `where` clauses | These rules apply to `where` clauses on any item. Directly after a closing bracket of any kind, **MUST** write `where` on the same line with a space before it; otherwise **MUST** put `where` on a new line at the same indentation level. |
| [RS-ITEM-15](02-items.md#rs-item-15) | Type aliases | **MUST** keep type aliases on one line when they fit; if a break is needed, break before the `=` and block-indent the right-hand side. |
| [RS-ITEM-16](02-items.md#rs-item-16) | Associated types | **MUST** format associated types like type aliases ([RS-ITEM-15](02-items.md#rs-item-15)). A bound on an associated type has a space after the colon but not before. |
| [RS-ITEM-17](02-items.md#rs-item-17) | Extern items | When writing extern items (such as `extern "C" fn`), **MUST** always specify the ABI. |
| [RS-ITEM-18](02-items.md#rs-item-18) | Imports (`use` statements) | Format imports on one line where possible. **MUST NOT** put spaces around braces. |
| [RS-ITEM-19](02-items.md#rs-item-19) | Large list imports | **SHOULD** prefer multiple imports to a multi-line import; however, tools **SHOULD NOT** split imports by default. |
| [RS-ITEM-20](02-items.md#rs-item-20) | Ordering of imports | Within a group of imports, imports **MUST** be version-sorted ([RS-FMT-06](01-formatting-conventions.md#rs-fmt-06)). Groups of imports **MUST NOT** be merged or re-ordered. |
| [RS-ITEM-21](02-items.md#rs-item-21) | Ordering list import | Names in a list import **MUST** be version-sorted, except that `self` and `super` always come first if present, and groups and glob imports always come last if present. |
| [RS-ITEM-22](02-items.md#rs-item-22) | Normalisation | Tools **MUST** make the following normalisations, recursively, and **MUST NOT** otherwise merge or un-merge import lists or adjust glob imports without an explicit option. |
| [RS-ITEM-23](02-items.md#rs-item-23) | Nested imports | If a list import contains any nested imports, **MUST** use the multi-line form even if it fits on one line. Each nested import goes on its own line; non-nested imports are grouped on as few lines as possible. |
| [RS-ITEM-24](02-items.md#rs-item-24) | Merging/un-merging imports | Tools **MUST NOT** merge or un-merge imports by default. They **MAY** offer merging or un-merging as an option. |

## [Statements](03-statements.md)

| ID | Title | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [RS-STMT-01](03-statements.md#rs-stmt-01) | Let statements | Put a space after the `:` and on both sides of the `=` (if present); **MUST NOT** put a space before the semicolon. Format the declaration on a single line if possible; otherwise break as described below, using block indentation. |
| [RS-STMT-02](03-statements.md#rs-stmt-02) | else blocks (let-else statements) | In a let-else statement, format the part before `else` (`let pattern: Type = initializer_expr`) exactly as other [let statements](03-statements.md#rs-stmt-01). When breaking across lines, **MUST NOT** break between `else` and `{`, and **MUST** always break before the `}`. |
| [RS-STMT-03](03-statements.md#rs-stmt-03) | Macros in statement position | A macro use in statement position **MUST** use parentheses or square brackets as delimiters and be terminated with a semicolon. **MUST NOT** put spaces around the name, `!`, the delimiters, or the `;`. |
| [RS-STMT-04](03-statements.md#rs-stmt-04) | Expressions in statement position | **MUST NOT** put a space between the expression and the semicolon. Terminate every expression in statement position with a semicolon, unless it ends with a block or is used as the value of a block. |

## [Expressions](04-expressions.md)

| ID | Title | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [RS-EXPR-01](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-01) | Blocks | A block expression **MUST** have a newline after the opening `{` and before the closing `}`, unless another rule allows it on a single line. A keyword before the block (e.g. `unsafe`, `async`) **MUST** be on the same line as the opening brace, separated by a single space. Indent the block contents. |
| [RS-EXPR-02](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-02) | Closures | **MUST NOT** put extra spaces before the first `\|` (unless prefixed by a keyword such as `move`); put a space between the second `\|` and the body. Between the `\|`s use function-definition syntax, eliding types where possible. Omit the enclosing `{}` where possible. |
| [RS-EXPR-03](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-03) | Struct literals | If a struct literal is *small*, format it on one line with no trailing comma; otherwise put each field on its own block-indented line with a trailing comma. |
| [RS-EXPR-04](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-04) | Unit literals | **MUST NOT** break between the parentheses of the `()` unit literal, even when the `)` would exceed the maximum line width. |
| [RS-EXPR-05](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-05) | Tuple literals | Use a single-line form where possible: no spaces after `(` or before `)`, elements separated by `, `. Otherwise put each element on its own block-indented line with a trailing comma. |
| [RS-EXPR-06](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-06) | Tuple struct literals | **MUST NOT** put a space between the identifier and `(`; otherwise follow [tuple literal](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-05) rules. |
| [RS-EXPR-07](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-07) | Enum literals | Follow the rules for the corresponding struct literal form. **SHOULD** qualify variants with the enum name, unless the enum is in the prelude. |
| [RS-EXPR-08](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-08) | Array literals | Write small array literals on one line: no spaces after `[` or before `]`, elements separated by `, `. With the repeat initializer, put a space after the `;` only. Apply the same rules to `vec!` and similar array-like macros, which **MUST** always use square brackets. |
| [RS-EXPR-09](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-09) | Array accesses, indexing, and slicing | **MUST NOT** put spaces around the square brackets. **SHOULD** avoid line breaks; **MUST NOT** break between the target expression and `[`. |
| [RS-EXPR-10](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-10) | Unary operations | **MUST NOT** put a space between a unary operator and its operand (`!x`, not `! x`), except that `&mut` **MUST** be followed by a space. **SHOULD** avoid breaking between a unary operator and its operand. |
| [RS-EXPR-11](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-11) | Binary operations | Put spaces around binary operators (`x + 1`, not `x+1`), including `=` and compound assignment operators (`+=`, `*=`, ...). |
| [RS-EXPR-12](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-12) | Casts (`as`) | Format `as` like a binary operator: always spaces around `as`; when breaking, break before `as` (never after) and block-indent the next line. Format the target type using the [type rules](05-types-and-bounds.md). |
| [RS-EXPR-13](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-13) | Control flow | **MUST NOT** add extraneous parentheses around `if` and `while` conditions. |
| [RS-EXPR-14](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-14) | Function calls | **MUST NOT** put a space between the function name and `(`, or between an argument and its following comma; put a space after each comma before the next argument. **SHOULD NOT** break inside the callee expression. |
| [RS-EXPR-15](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-15) | Single-line calls | **MUST NOT** put a space between the function name and `(`, after `(`, or before `)`. **MUST NOT** put a comma after the last argument. |
| [RS-EXPR-16](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-16) | Multi-line calls | Format a call across multiple lines if it is not *small*, would exceed the max width, or any argument or the callee is multi-line. Then put each argument on its own block-indented line, break after `(` and before `)`, and use a trailing comma. |
| [RS-EXPR-17](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-17) | Method calls | Follow the [function call](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-14) rules. **MUST NOT** put spaces around the `.`. |
| [RS-EXPR-18](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-18) | Macro uses | If a macro use can be parsed like another construct, format it like that construct (e.g. `foo!(a, b, c)` parses like a function call ignoring the `!`, so use [function call](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-14) rules). |
| [RS-EXPR-19](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-19) | Format string macros | For macros taking a format string, if all other arguments are *small*, put the arguments before the format string on one line if they fit, the format string on its own line, and the arguments after it on one line if they fit. If arguments are not small or don't fit, put each on its own line as for a function call. |
| [RS-EXPR-20](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-20) | Chains of fields and method calls | A chain is a sequence of field accesses, method calls and/or `?` (e.g. `a.b.c().d`, `foo?.bar().baz?`). Format it on one line if it is *small* and otherwise possible; else put each field access or method call on its own block-indented line, breaking before the `.` and after any `?`. |
| [RS-EXPR-21](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-21) | Multi-line chain elements | If any chain element is formatted across multiple lines, put that element and all later elements on their own lines. **SHOULD** prefer the whole chain in multi-line style with each element on one line over mixing single-line and multi-line elements. |
| [RS-EXPR-22](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-22) | Control flow expressions | Applies to `for`, `loop`, `if` and `while` expressions, including `if let`/`while let` and let-chains (one or more `let` sub-expressions plus one or more bool conditions, e.g. `if a && let Some(b) = c`). Put the keyword, initial clauses and opening brace on one line if they fit; format the block per [block rules](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-01). |
| [RS-EXPR-23](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-23) | Single line `if else` | Put an `if else` or `if let else` on a single line if it is in expression context (not a standalone statement), has a single `else` clause, and is *small*. |
| [RS-EXPR-24](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-24) | Match | **SHOULD NOT** break inside the discriminant expression. **MUST** always break after `{` and before `}`, and block-indent the arms once. Use a trailing comma on an arm if and only if it does not use a block. **MUST NOT** start an arm pattern with `\|`. |
| [RS-EXPR-25](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-25) | Match arm line-breaking | If using a block body on the right-hand side avoids breaking the left-hand side, **SHOULD** do that. **MUST NOT** break after `=>` without using the block form of the body. |
| [RS-EXPR-26](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-26) | Combinable expressions | When a function call has a single argument formatted across multiple lines, format the outer call as if single-line if the result fits. Apply the same combining to similar constructs with multi-line, block-indented, parenthesis-delimited sub-expression lists (e.g. macros, tuple struct literals). Apply recursively. |
| [RS-EXPR-27](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-27) | Ranges | **MUST NOT** put spaces in ranges (`0..10`, `x..=y`, `..x.len()`, `foo..`). If either bound is a compound expression, parenthesize it to show precedence (`..(x + 1)`, `(x.f)..(x.f.len())`, `0..(x - 10)`). |
| [RS-EXPR-28](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-28) | Hexadecimal literals | Hex literals **MAY** use upper- or lower-case letters but **MUST NOT** mix cases within one literal. Projects **SHOULD** use the same case for all literals; the style guide recommends neither case. |
| [RS-EXPR-29](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-29) | Patterns | Format patterns like their corresponding expressions. See [Match](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-24) and [match arm line-breaking](04-expressions.md#rs-expr-25) for match-arm pattern formatting. |

## [Types and Bounds](05-types-and-bounds.md)

| ID | Title | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [RS-TYPE-01](05-types-and-bounds.md#rs-type-01) | Single line formatting | Format types on a single line with the spacing below. **MUST NOT** put spaces around parentheses used in types, e.g. `(Foo)`. |
| [RS-TYPE-02](05-types-and-bounds.md#rs-type-02) | Line breaks | **SHOULD** avoid breaking lines in types where possible; when a break is needed, **SHOULD** prefer breaking at the outermost scope. |
| [RS-TYPE-03](05-types-and-bounds.md#rs-type-03) | Precise capturing bounds | Format a `use<'a, T>` precise capturing bound as if it were a single path segment with non-turbofished angle-bracketed args, i.e. like a trait bound whose identifier is `use`. |

## [Other Style Advice](06-other-style-advice.md)

| ID | Title | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [RS-ADV-01](06-other-style-advice.md#rs-adv-01) | Expressions | **SHOULD** use Rust's expression-oriented nature where possible. |
| [RS-ADV-02](06-other-style-advice.md#rs-adv-02) | Names | Names **MUST** follow the case conventions below. When a name is forbidden because it is a reserved word, use a raw identifier or a trailing underscore; **MUST NOT** misspell the word. |
| [RS-ADV-03](06-other-style-advice.md#rs-adv-03) | Modules | **SHOULD** avoid `#[path]` annotations where possible. |

## [Cargo.toml Conventions](07-cargo-toml.md)

| ID | Title | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [RS-CARGO-01](07-cargo-toml.md#rs-cargo-01) | Formatting conventions | Use the same line width and indentation as Rust code, and lay out sections, keys, strings, arrays and tables as detailed below. |
| [RS-CARGO-02](07-cargo-toml.md#rs-cargo-02) | Metadata conventions | Metadata fields follow the conventions below for `authors`, `license`, `homepage` and `description`. |

## [Guiding Principles and Rationale](08-guiding-principles.md)

| ID | Title | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [RS-PRIN-01](08-guiding-principles.md#rs-prin-01) | Readability | Readability is the highest-priority principle. |
| [RS-PRIN-02](08-guiding-principles.md#rs-prin-02) | Aesthetics | Aesthetics rank second, after readability. |
| [RS-PRIN-03](08-guiding-principles.md#rs-prin-03) | Specifics | Specifics rank third. |
| [RS-PRIN-04](08-guiding-principles.md#rs-prin-04) | Application | Application concerns rank fourth. |

## [Rust Style Editions](09-style-editions.md)

| ID | Title | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [RS-ED-01](09-style-editions.md#rs-ed-01) | Rust next style edition | **MUST NOT** break within a nullary function call `func()` or a unit literal `()`. *Applies to: the next (post-2024) style edition.* |
| [RS-ED-02](09-style-editions.md#rs-ed-02) | Rust 2024 style edition | This style guide describes the Rust 2024 style edition, which (per the source) is currently nightly-only and may change before the release of Rust 2024. *Applies to: Rust 2024 style edition.* |
| [RS-ED-03](09-style-editions.md#rs-ed-03) | Rust 2015/2018/2021 style edition | The style edition shared by Rust 2015, Rust 2018 and Rust 2021 is described by the [archived style guide](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/tree/37343f4a4d4ed7ad0891cb79e8eb25acf43fb821/src/doc/style-guide/src). *Applies to: Rust 2015, 2018 and 2021 style edition.* |

## [Nightly-only Syntax](10-nightly-only-syntax.md)

| ID | Title | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [RS-NIGHT-01](10-nightly-only-syntax.md#rs-night-01) | Frontmatter | **SHOULD NOT** put blank lines between the frontmatter and either the start of the file or a shebang; there **MAY** be zero or one line between the frontmatter and any following content. Fences **SHOULD** use the minimum number of dashes needed. *Applies to: nightly only; feature gate `frontmatter`; tracking issue [#136889](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/136889). Location: placed before comments and attributes in the [root](01-formatting-conventions.md).* |
